title: SeamDefinition
description: VENDORED from SourceOS-Linux/sourceos-spec (T0-2, canonical owner). A typed architectural seam: an ungated boundary between two system layers that represents an attack surface. Seams are the estate's threat-model spine — each names where trust is not yet enforced, the vector that exploits it, and the gate that would close it. Canonical instance URN: urn:srcos:seam-definition:<seam_id_slug>. Schema version 1.0.0.

type.description: Object discriminator, matching the repo convention (examples are mapped to their schema by this field). Optional.

seam_id.description: Stable seam identifier, e.g. SEAM-013. Slugged into the URN urn:srcos:seam-definition:<seam_id_slug>.

boundary_from.description: The layer the seam originates at (e.g. MDM).

boundary_to.description: The layer the seam crosses into (e.g. usernoted).

attack_vector.description: How the ungated boundary is exploited.

known_exploits.description: Concrete observed exploits or indicators for this seam.

gate_requirements.description: What must be enforced to close the seam. Required and non-empty: a seam with no stated gate is not actionable.

linked_repos.description: Repos (and optionally issues) that own the gate work.

first_identified.description: Date the seam was first identified.

last_reviewed.description: Date the seam was last reviewed.
